title: Calculus bovis inhibits M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization via Wnt/beta-catenin pathway modulation to suppress liver cancer.
authors: Huang, Zhen; Meng, Fan-Ying; Lu, Lin-Zhu; Guo, Qian-Qian; Lv, Chang-Jun; Tan, Nian-Hua; Deng, Zhe; Chen, Jun-Yi; Zhang, Zi-Shu; Zou, Bo; Long, Hong-Ping; Zhou, Qing; Tian, Sha; Mei, Si; Tian, Xue-Fei
one_liner_zh: 研究牛黄通过Wnt/β-catenin通路抑制M2型肿瘤相关巨噬细胞极化以治疗肝癌，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，方法以实验为主，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Calculus bovis (CB), used in traditional Chinese medicine, exhibits anti-tumor effects in various cancer models. It also constitutes an integral component of a compound formulation known as Pien Tze Huang, which is indicated for the treatment of liver cancer. However, its impact on the liver cancer tumor microenvironment, particularly on tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), is not well understood. AIM: To elucidate the anti-liver cancer effect of CB by inhibiting M2-TAM polarization via Wnt/beta-catenin pathway modulation. METHODS: This study identified the active components of CB using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, evaluated its anti-neoplastic effects in a nude mouse model, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms via network pharmacology, transcriptomics, and molecular docking. In vitro assays were used to investigate the effects of CB-containing serum on HepG2 cells and M2-TAMs, and Wnt pathway modulation was validated by real-time reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction and Western blot analysis. RESULTS: This study identified 22 active components in CB, 11 of which were detected in the bloodstream. Preclinical investigations have demonstrated the ability of CB to effectively inhibit liver tumor growth. An integrated approach employing network pharmacology, transcriptomics, and molecular docking implicated the Wnt signaling pathway as a target of the antineoplastic activity of CB by suppressing M2-TAM polarization. In vitro and in vivo experiments further confirmed that CB significantly hinders M2-TAM polarization and suppresses Wnt/beta-catenin pathway activation. The inhibitory effect of CB on M2-TAMs was reversed when treated with the Wnt agonist SKL2001, confirming its pathway specificity. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that CB mediates inhibition of M2-TAM polarization through the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, contributing to the suppression of liver cancer growth.
abstract_zh: 背景：牛黄（Calculus bovis, CB）作为传统中药，在各种癌症模型中表现出抗肿瘤作用。它也是名为片仔癀的复方制剂的重要组成部分，该制剂被指示用于治疗肝癌。然而，其对肝癌肿瘤微环境，特别是肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（tumor-associated macrophages, TAMs）的影响，尚不十分清楚。目的：阐明CB通过调节Wnt/β-catenin通路抑制M2型TAM极化从而发挥抗肝癌作用。方法：本研究利用UPLC-Q-TOF-MS鉴定了CB的活性成分，在裸鼠模型中评估了其抗肿瘤效应，并通过网络药理学、转录组学和分子对接阐明了潜在机制。体外实验用于研究含CB血清对HepG2细胞和M2型TAMs的影响，并通过实时逆转录聚合酶链反应和Western blot分析验证了Wnt通路调节。结果：本研究在CB中鉴定出22种活性成分，其中11种在血液中被检测到。临床前研究证明CB能有效抑制肝脏肿瘤生长。采用网络药理学、转录组学和分子对接的综合方法表明，Wnt信号通路是CB通过抑制M2型TAM极化发挥抗肿瘤活性的靶点。体外和体内实验进一步证实，CB显著阻碍M2型TAM极化并抑制Wnt/β-catenin通路激活。当用Wnt激动剂SKL2001处理时，CB对M2型TAMs的抑制作用被逆转，确认了其通路特异性。结论：本研究证明CB通过Wnt/β-catenin通路介导抑制M2型TAM极化，从而有助于抑制肝癌生长。
